text:
kevin: hey all, day 2 here. trying to get dev env consistent. i installed homebrew on my M1 and asdf. still seeing python coming from /usr/bin when i open VSCode integrated terminal. normal iTerm has the right pyenv/asdf python. any ideas?

ria: welcome! :wave: most likely VSCode terminal isn't a login shell so it doesn't source ~/.zprofile where you put PATH/asdf init. check your VSCode setting `terminal.integrated.profiles.osx` or set `terminal.integrated.shellArgs.osx` to `['-l']` to force login shell.

kevin: ah that makes sense. i had asdf init in .zprofile. is there a minimal set for zsh so both GUI and terminal panes work?

dev-mentor: quick pattern we've used: keep PATH and asdf init in ~/.zprofile, and in ~/.zshrc add a tiny guard to source zprofile for non-login interactive shells: 

if [ -f "$HOME/.zprofile" ] && [ -z "$ZSH_EVAL_CONTEXT" ]; then
  source "$HOME/.zprofile"
fi

but simpler is to configure VSCode to use login shells like ria said.

kevin: another thing: pip (global) installs try to write to /Library/Python/3.9 and i get permission errors. we use a mix of poetry and asdf python. what's the recommended approach?

ria: prefer isolated envs: use `python -m venv` or poetry. make sure `pip` you're invoking is the one from the asdf python. `which -a pip python` helps. for global tools (black, pre-commit) we usually install them into a virtualenv or put a tools env under ~/.local/bin and add that to PATH. avoid sudo pip.

kevin: got it. last odd bit: my Docker-based test runner can't see REACT_APP_* env vars from .env.local when run in VSCode test runner but works in Terminal. any known quirks?

dev-mentor: VSCode test runner and some extensions launch processes without loading your shell env. we recommend using direnv for per-project envs and committing `.envrc` that exports vars for local dev (but keep secrets out). add `use dotenv` or `layout node` where appropriate. also point dev vs code run config to use "envFile": "${workspaceFolder}/.env.local" in launch.json or set env in the task.

kevin: we have direnv in the dotfiles repo?

ria: yes, we have a small shared dotfiles: https://git.internal/redwood/dotfiles with a sample .envrc and a README on trusting direnv. ops-bot also enforces not to commit secrets.

ops-bot: Reminder: do not commit credentials. Use the secrets manager (1Password) + the repo's secret sync script: https://internal.redwood.dev/secrets. If you need access to infra creds, request via #infra-requests.

kevin: thanks all. last micro-optimization Q: should i install node via asdf or brew? our CI uses node 18 LTS.

ria: we standardize dev versions with asdf so everyone gets same shims and `asdf local` files. it reduces the "works on my machine" issues. brew is fine for system tooling but not for app runtimes we pin.

kevin: perfect. i'll switch node to asdf, reshim, and update VSCode shell args. appreciate the quick help :thumbsup:
